comment: Edit decision list for the AI-in-the-lab highlights compilation. All clip times are seconds on the ORIGINAL 75:34 recording timeline (see ../README.md). Rendered by make_highlights.py. 2026-08-24 fix: boundaries are word-aligned to faster-whisper word onsets (>=0.3-0.5 s pre-roll before each opening word, cuts placed in real speech gaps) -- the original cut used Teams cue times, which lag the audio by ~0.5-1.2 s and clipped the start of most segments' first sentence. 2026-08-24 breakouts: adds Part 05 with bites from the seven break-off pair-discussion clips (edl['sources']); those piece times are seconds on each clip's own timeline. Most in-person pairs set the phone face-up while recording ('Don't film me'), so their bites render as navy audio-cards with a live waveform; captions come from whisper VTTs in sources/. 2026-08-29: delivery audio raised from 16 kHz mono / 96 kbps undenoised to 48 kHz / 160 kbps with the reels' noise-reduction chain, and the sidecar captions made a real caption track (no overlaps, <=42-char lines, speaker tags) -- ../best-practices/ findings 1, 3 and 4.

audio.denoise: highpass 85 Hz -> RNNoise (arnndn, sh.rnnn) -> afftdn -> 3 kHz presence -> lowpass 12 kHz -> gentle compression, applied to a 2 s pre-rolled window of continuous source ahead of each cut (ported from ../reels/ 2026-08-29)

items.why: Carl's thesis is the punchiest half-minute of the meeting, opened at the top of the thought: 'the biggest thing is just recognizing that we're going to have AI forever' through 'if that's all you use, you're useless, because anyone can use AI.'

items.kicker: BYU VERTICAL CLOUD LAB · GROUP MEETING · AUGUST 19, 2026
items.title: AI in the lab

items.why: Sterling reads the three prompts that structure the whole meeting (screen share). Interior trim removes silent scrolling.

items.title: Exhibit A: @claude runs a sensor test

items.why: Concrete artifact on screen: Tim's @claude comment that picked up the enclosure, ran the Colab test, and posted results. Interior trim removes silent scrolling.
The meeting's signature analogy: complacency vs. competency. Interior trim (26:39-27:15) drops an aside; kept through the mountain-biking landing.
The counterpoint, with the laugh line 'sorry, I bought it for everybody': you cannot choose not to buy this e-bike, so competent-and-fruitful use is the real question.
The Tony Stark framing: Jarvis is a support to Tony Stark, not doing Tony Stark's work.

Writing the paper yourself vs. backtracking through AI output, from 'I know the difference of myself personally' to the rhetorical 'is this right? is this right?'. Interior trim removes a garbled aside.

items.label: Andrew & Marcus
items.why: The eleven seconds that explain this whole section: villain fingertip-steeple, 'Lab culture. Death and destruction.' -- and 'Don't film me,' after which their phone spends the rest of the clip face-up on the table. Hence the audio-cards that follow.
The section thesis in their own words: 'we're supposed to be things that act and not to be acted upon -- if we start using AI too much, AI starts using us.'

items.topic: on what AI still can't do
items.why: Twelve-second limit report that rhymes with Audrey's 'it doesn't live in the 3D world with us' in the next part: 'it's funny how bad AI's spatial reasoning is.'

items.label: Gage & Ronnie · positive experiences
items.why: Concrete win, on camera: AI taught them why elemental powders are explosion risks and aluminum alloys are the safer form -- learning, not delegating.

items.topic: on making AI critique your ideas
items.why: The most actionable pattern of the breakouts: give it a baseline and have it critique your ideas -- 'that will help you think as well while you're using AI.'

items.topic: on learning from the ground up
items.why: Ben built the machine from the ground up and worries the next cohort won't get the chance -- sets up both the Xavier & Sam confession and Audrey's onboarding item.

items.label: Xavier & Sam · experiences with AI
items.why: The worry made flesh, said out loud on camera: Claude runs the powder doser end to end; 'if you asked me to do it myself, I couldn't do it right now... that's scary.'

items.topic: on knowing it, not just generating it
items.why: The antidote, observed in the wild: 'I could tell that Xavier really understood -- he wasn't just using AI to do the learning.'

items.label: Xavier & Sam · experiences with AI
items.why: Closes the section on the thesis that echoes Carl's cold open: 'if Claude is doing research, then anybody can push the button -- my research should have aspects of me in it.'
Audrey: figuring out what is actually grunt work -- months on generative CAD, 'and that's okay, plenty of us enjoy doing CAD.' Carl's 'that was a rant' lands underneath.
The exchange: Carl's 'very good at image analysis, spatial analysis ... it's not there yet' answered by Audrey's 'it doesn't live in the 3D world with us. It's all just code and stuff.'

pieces.cap_last_text: It's all just code and stuff.

items.why: The pair lands the culture question in two voices, entering on Audrey's 'okay, yeah, no, I can see that': 'I'm probably overusing it' / 'and probably under-using it, so we just need to...'
Reconvene levity that explains where the channel clips came from: 'we are about to get YouTube famous.'
Audrey's concrete action item: teach good AI patterns during onboarding; 'we need some kind of tutorial to show people.'

pieces.cap_last_text: and using it to maybe like debug stuff.

items.why: Sterling: 'we could make a reel of us -- this is good, this is bad.' This compilation is that artifact.
The natural close: 'Okay, we'll probably call it good there. Thanks, Audrey, Carl. Thanks, everybody.'
